text.tspan: Potassium (position 1) is MORE reactive than Zn (position 6). The more
reactive metal displaces the less reactive metal from its compound.
This happens because Potassium has a stronger tendency to lose
electrons and form positive ions. It "pushes out" the Zn atoms,
which then precipitate as solid metal.
